title: Canonical integers and common counts (mathematical Lines)
description: Each entry is a Line as a whole number: an integer count that reaches from 0 out along the number line. Where /1 (Longs) reads a magnitude as a length series over time, /5 (Lines) reads a magnitude as a plain count or extent. These are EXACT — an integer is defined, not measured.

provenance.primary_source: Standard mathematics (public domain); OEIS for sequence identifiers
provenance.cross_reference: OEIS (oeis.org) sequence numbers cited where applicable
provenance.note: Values are definitional integers. A count is a Line laid out unit by unit; EXACT means no uncertainty and no date. Integers are alphabetized by name for reader ease.
